source_name: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No.712 of 18.06.2025 — procedure for developing/approving security profiles and security authorisation (kmu.gov.ua)
why_relevant: Implements Law 4336-IX: defines basic, sectoral and target security profiles (basic profiles approved by SSSCIP) and the security-authorisation procedure. Sectoral profiles are the mechanism by which banking/payment infrastructure gets its own binding technical baseline and dates.

source_name: CMU Resolution No.518 of 19.06.2019 — General requirements for cyber defence of critical infrastructure objects (LigaZakon copy)
source_subtype: commercial legal database copy of a government act
why_relevant: The baseline 'Загальні вимоги до кіберзахисту об'єктів критичної інфраструктури' that banks as CI operators must meet; updated versions impose mandatory basic measures, continuous cyber-risk management, a cybersecurity plan, staff training and funding. Directly generates compliance-driven demand.

source_name: Verkhovna Rada Ombudsman — personal data protection directorate, inspections and clarifications
why_relevant: Ukraine's current personal-data supervisory authority (since 2014). Publishes controller/processor obligations, clarifications, and — critically — inspection results, which reveal enforcement posture towards banks and other large data controllers ahead of the GDPR-style reform.

source_name: Verkhovna Rada bill card #8153 — draft Law on Personal Data Protection (itd.rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The GDPR-alignment data-protection bill (passed first reading) that would create an independent supervisory authority and reshape banks' lawful-basis, DPO and breach-notification duties. The bill card is the canonical status/stage tracker with dates.

source_name: Kibberbez / cybersec.net.ua — Ukrainian cybersecurity trade outlet, normative documents section
why_relevant: Specialist Ukrainian-language trade press that reliably summarises new SSSCIP/CMU cyber acts, including updated CI cyber-defence requirements and the security-profile procedures. Useful as an early pointer and as plain-language interpretation of deadlines.

source_name: Deloitte Ukraine — tax and legal alerts (cyber/data compliance for financial institutions)
why_relevant: Big-four alerts translate NBU/SSSCIP acts into scoped obligations and compliance dates for financial institutions, and flag DORA alignment. High signal on what regulated entities will actually have to buy and by when.

source_name: Independent Association of Ukrainian Banks (NABU) — draft NBU act commentary page
why_relevant: Banking industry association that circulates NBU draft resolutions to members and aggregates comments during consultation windows. Reveals industry pushback and likely amendments to information-security requirements before adoption.

source_name: Ukrainian Association of Payment Systems (UAPS) — cyber resilience training and sector news
why_relevant: PSP-side association; covers cyber-resilience programmes for the banking/payments sector and how payment participants are implementing NBU security requirements. Useful for the PSP half of the cell, which NBU-only sources under-cover.

source_name: National Cybersecurity Coordination Centre (NCCC) at the NSDC — rnbo.gov.ua activity section
why_relevant: Coordinating body whose NSDC decisions (enacted by presidential decrees) set the Cybersecurity Strategy implementation plan and inter-agency tasking that later becomes binding SSSCIP/NBU rules. Also convenes the Kyiv International Cyber Resilience Forum, a signalling venue.

source_name: SSSCIP IT & cybersecurity qualification centre (qc.csi.cip.gov.ua)
why_relevant: Publishes professional standards and certification requirements for critical-infrastructure protection specialists — an indirect but leading indicator of mandatory staffing/competence obligations that will land on banks and PSPs as CI operators.

source_name: EU4Digital — Ukraine critical infrastructure cybersecurity alignment with EU standards
why_relevant: EU-funded programme reporting on Ukraine's NIS2/DORA-direction alignment and donor-funded capacity building. Useful for anticipating which EU instruments Ukrainian rules will copy next and where donor money for security tooling is flowing.

source_name: Legalink / Lexology legal alerts on Ukraine's new cybersecurity law
why_relevant: English-language law-firm analysis of Law 4336-IX naming SSSCIP's powers (basic and sectoral security profiles, incident repository, supervision) — the fastest way to brief non-Ukrainian-speaking stakeholders and to map obligations onto payment operators.

source_name: КІС НБУ — Комплексна інформаційна система (online registers of non-bank financial institutions)
why_relevant: NBU's searchable online system holding the Державний реєстр фінансових установ and the Реєстр осіб, які не є фінансовими установами, але мають право надавати окремі фінансові послуги. This is the authoritative live lookup surface for non-bank PSPs, finance companies, pawnshops and e-money-adjacent actors — the single richest actor-enumeration entry point outside the bank list.

source_name: data.gov.ua — Державний реєстр фінансових установ (DRFU dataset, NBU as data holder)
why_relevant: Machine-readable export of the State Register of Financial Institutions (insurers, credit unions, finance companies, pawnshops) published as an open dataset with a stable XLSX resource and CKAN metadata. Explicitly documented as refreshed automatically twice a month (1st and 16th), which makes it a low-friction change-detection feed for the regulated non-bank population.

source_name: data.gov.ua CKAN API (national open data portal API)
why_relevant: The portal's own user documentation states datasets are retrievable via https://data.gov.ua/api/3/action/package_show?id=[identifier]. Standard CKAN gives package_search, organization_show and resource metadata — the cheapest programmatic route to every Ukrainian state register published as open data, including NBU's.

source_name: NBU REST API OpenData / NBUStatService (statdirectory)
why_relevant: NBU's own machine-readable service exposing statistical directories and data blocks in XML/JSON, including reference dictionaries (довідники) used for statistical reporting. Directory endpoints frequently carry the code lists of banks and reporting entities, making this both a data feed and an identifier crosswalk for the register work.

source_name: NBU — Довідник банків та їх відокремлених підрозділів (bank & branch directory API)
why_relevant: The canonical NBU directory of licensed banks and their separate subdivisions, with an official API instruction document. This is the authoritative legal-name + MFO/EDRPOU code list of the Ukrainian bank population — the backbone identifier table for every other workstream.

source_name: NBU — Ліцензування небанківських установ / Licensing of non-bank institutions (EN + UA)
why_relevant: Hub for authorisation of financial payment service providers and limited payment service providers under NBU Board Resolution No. 217 of 07.10.2022. Links application forms, decision lists and the register entries — the procedural map that explains what an RPI/register entry means and when it changes.

source_name: NBU newsroom — licence-grant announcements for payment services (e.g. 'Ще вісім учасників ринку отримали ліцензії')
why_relevant: NBU publishes each batch of new payment-service licences as a news item naming the licensees. This is the fastest-moving, name-bearing signal of register changes and typically precedes the register file refresh — an ideal high-frequency tripwire feeding the actor map.

source_name: Фонд гарантування вкладів фізичних осіб — Банки в управлінні Фонду (Deposit Guarantee Fund: banks under administration/liquidation)
why_relevant: The authoritative list of insolvent, resolved and liquidated Ukrainian banks, split into sub-registers (temporary administration, in liquidation, liquidated, sold to investors/state) plus a list of agent banks. It is the negative image of the NBU bank licence list and is required to keep the actor map from carrying dead institutions.

source_name: Державний реєстр санкцій (NSDC State Register of Sanctions)
why_relevant: Official searchable register of all persons and entities under Ukrainian sanctions, maintained by the NSDC Office and synchronised with presidential decrees and court rulings. Essential for filtering the payments/banking actor population and for detecting when a PSP, processor or shareholder becomes sanctioned. Offers official electronic extracts (витяг).

source_name: OpenSanctions — Ukraine NSDC State Register of Sanctions dataset
why_relevant: Normalised, versioned, bulk-downloadable mirror of the Ukrainian sanctions register with stable entity schemas and identifiers. Removes the need to scrape drs.nsdc.gov.ua and makes cross-matching against bank/PSP legal names tractable.

source_name: data.gov.ua — Єдиний державний реєстр юридичних осіб, ФОП та громадських формувань (EDR open dataset, Ministry of Justice)
why_relevant: The master company register of Ukraine, restored to open-data publication on 19 January 2026 after wartime restriction. Provides EDRPOU codes, legal names, addresses and status for every bank, PSP and processor found in the NBU registers — the join key that turns register names into a queryable corporate graph.

source_name: data.gov.ua — tag-filtered discovery views (небанківська фінансова установа / фінансова)
why_relevant: Tag-based facets on the national portal act as a cheap, repeatable discovery loop for financial-sector datasets across all publishers (NBU, Ministry of Justice, NSSMC, Ministry of Finance), surfacing register datasets that are never linked from the regulators' own sites.

source_name: diia.data.gov.ua — Де знайти відкриті дані (open data portal directory)
why_relevant: State-run index of Ukrainian open-data portals beyond data.gov.ua (regional portals, sectoral portals, agency portals). Pure source-discovery surface for finding register mirrors and secondary publication points when a primary register goes dark.

source_name: regulation.gov.ua — catalogue of state functions and permits (NBU register-keeping function id5592)
why_relevant: State deregulation portal cataloguing each regulator's statutory functions and the permits attached to them, including NBU's duty to keep the register of payment systems, settlement systems, their participants and payment-infrastructure service operators. Reveals the legal basis, permit types and procedural deadlines behind each register entry — a structural map of the licensing surface.

source_name: zakon.rada.gov.ua — NBU register regulations (Положення про реєстрацію платіжних систем, учасників та технологічних операторів)
why_relevant: Official legal database entry for the amendments to the NBU regulation governing what goes into the Register of Payment Infrastructure and on what timetable. Defines the register's fields, inclusion/exclusion grounds and statutory deadlines — required to interpret register diffs correctly rather than guessing.

source_name: НКЦПФР / NSSMC — licensing and registration registers (including State Register of Financial Institutions view)
why_relevant: The securities regulator maintains its own slice of the financial-institution register (asset managers, depositories, traders). Adjacent to but distinct from the NBU population; needed so the actor map does not misattribute capital-markets entities to NBU supervision, and it also republishes sanctions-register notices.
